# ezghcloud_hosted_queue_rabbitmq_policy (Resource)

A policy on a RabbitMQ cluster's vhost. Destroying it deletes this policy alone.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster (hqc_) it is in. Changing it replaces the object.
- `definition` (String) The policy as a JSON object (jsonencode) of max-length, max-length-bytes, message-ttl, expires, overflow, dead-letter-exchange, dead-letter-routing-key, delivery-limit or queue-leader-locator. Changes in place.
- `name` (String) The policy's name. Changing it replaces the object.
- `pattern` (String) Regular expression matched against queue and exchange names. Changes in place.
- `project_id` (String) Project of the cluster. Changing it replaces the object.
- `vhost` (String) The vhost it is in: / (or default) for the default vhost. Changing it replaces the object.

### Optional

- `apply_to` (String) all, queues, exchanges, classic_queues, quorum_queues or streams. Changes in place.
- `priority` (Number) 0 to 999; the highest matching policy applies. Changes in place.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) cluster_id/name, with the vhost before the name for a RabbitMQ object.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `origin` (String) api if it was made through EZGH, broker if an app made it first (an imported object).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_hosted_queue_rabbitmq_policy.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/CLUSTER_ID/VHOST/NAME'
```
